utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: I can help with the repair drive this weekend—what still needs doing?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Mostly sorting donations and a couple of pickup runs, if you don’t mind. I’d appreciate the help.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: That works for me. I can handle a pickup run and help sort after—what time should I come by?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Before we commit, where are we storing the materials and who’s handling drop-off times if people aren’t home?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Can we confirm the storage spot first, and who’s actually coordinating drop-offs when folks aren’t home?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Exactly—that’s what I need nailed down first, because if we don’t have a secure storage spot and one person managing missed drop-offs, this could get messy fast.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh right, the repair drive—are we still doing it this weekend, or did that change?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: I think we’re still on for this weekend—unless I’m mixing it up with the park cleanup again. Maybe Saturday, if that sounds right to you?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Yeah, Saturday sounds familiar to me too, though I could be mixing it up as well. Maybe we should double-check with Mina before I show up with the wrong tools.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Ira, I’m telling everyone the repair drive’s coming up, so folks can bring their broken stuff by and help out.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Oh, that’s great—people have been meaning to fix things around here. I’ll spread the word while I’m out.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Perfect, and I’ll keep reminding people too—the repair drive’s coming up, so everyone should bring their broken stuff by and pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Gus, sorry I’m late again—how’s the repair drive looking so far?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: No worries, Dane—pretty good so far. We’ve got a small pile of toasters and lamps already, and I brought my tool kit in case we need it.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: That’s a solid start—glad you brought the kit. Where do you want me to jump in?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Let’s keep it simple, Quinn: make a list of the repairs, then we can line them up one by one for the drive.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Perfect, I’ll start a quick list and let the block know we’re lining up repairs for the drive one by one.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Good, that’s the right way to do it. Once you’ve got the list, bring it by and we’ll set a clear order for the drive.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Sam, how many volunteers have actually signed up for the repair drive so far?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: So far I’ve got six confirmed volunteers, and two more said they’d let me know by tonight.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Six confirmed is a start—do we have enough people to cover intake, repairs, and cleanup, or do we need to ask around some more?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: I’m glad you brought up the repair drive, Opal — it feels like the perfect chance to get everyone working together. Who have you already looped in?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: So far I’ve looped in Mara at the corner house, Ben from across the alley, and the Nguyens on Cedar—they all said they can stop by if we set up near the community garden.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That’s a great start — the community garden is perfect because folks from both sides of the block pass through there. I can reach out to Tessa and Omar too, since they’re both good at pulling in a few more hands.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Hi Rosa — I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive; I want to help make sure it runs smoothly.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That means a lot, Mara—thank you. I’m pulling together a simple plan now, and I’d love your help with check-in and keeping volunteers organized.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Absolutely, Rosa—I can handle check-in and help keep the volunteers organized. If you want, we can go over the flow together so I know exactly what you need.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ve got a running list of what we’ve got for the repair drive, Bo. Tell me what’s still needed and I’ll check our supplies.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: We still need more extension cords, duct tape, and work gloves, I think. If you’ve got spare tarps too, those would help.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ve got duct tape covered and one spare tarp, but we’re short on extension cords and work gloves. I’ll mark those as the priority asks for the drive.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hey Rey, have you heard anything new about the repair drive yet? I’ve been asking around and folks seem pretty eager to get it sorted.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Not much yet—just that people seem ready to pitch in once there’s a date. If I hear anything solid, I’ll let you know.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, that’s good to hear—sounds like we won’t be short on help once it’s set. If I catch wind of a date first, I’ll come straight by and tell you.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Before we set anything up, what exactly needs repairing and who’s already volunteered to help?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Mostly bikes and a couple of wobbly scooters from the school run crowd, plus one stroller brake that needs a look. So far I’ve got Amir for tools, Denise for check-in, and I can stay through pickup if we do it after school.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: That helps—do we know roughly how many bikes and scooters to expect, and whether anyone there can handle the stroller brake safely?
